transcript.heading: News Report One (British Male)
paras: A major art museum in New York City announced yesterday that it has successfully recovered a valuable painting that was stolen from its collection more than 30 years ago. The painting, a 19th-century landscape by a famous French impressionist, was valued at approximately 15 million dollars. It disappeared from the museum in 1992 during a renovation project, and investigators had been searching for it ever since. The breakthrough came when an art dealer in Italy contacted the museum after noticing inconsistencies in the painting's documentation when a private collector attempted to sell it. Working with Italian law enforcement and Interpol, museum officials verified the painting's authenticity through a combination of forensic analysis and matching its unique catalog markings. The painting is currently being restored and is expected to go back on public display early next year as part of a special exhibition about recovered artworks. Museum directors expressed their gratitude to the international law enforcement agencies that assisted in the recovery, calling it a victory for cultural heritage preservation worldwide.

transcript.heading: News Report Two (American Female)
paras: The United States Department of Agriculture has issued new dietary guidelines that emphasize plant-based foods and reduced sugar consumption for Americans of all ages. The updated guidelines, which are revised every five years, recommend that adults consume at least five servings of fruits and vegetables daily and limit added sugars to less than 10 percent of daily caloric intake. For the first time, the guidelines also include specific recommendations for infants and toddlers, advising against introducing added sugars to children under the age of two. Nutrition experts say the new guidelines reflect growing scientific evidence linking diets high in processed foods and added sugars to chronic conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease. The guidelines also encourage consumption of whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats such as those found in nuts and olive oil. While the recommendations have been widely praised by public health organizations, some food industry groups have criticized them as being too restrictive and difficult for average families to follow. The USDA plans to launch a nationwide educational campaign to help people incorporate the guidelines into their daily meal planning.

transcript.heading: News Report Three (American Male)
paras: A high-speed rail line connecting two major cities in Japan has set a new world record for the fastest train journey during a test run last week. The magnetic levitation train, known as a maglev, reached a top speed of 603 kilometers per hour, breaking the previous record of 581 kilometers per hour set by the same train model in 2015. The test was conducted on an experimental track in Yamanashi Prefecture as part of preparations for a new commercial maglev line scheduled to open between Tokyo and Nagoya in 2027. Maglev trains use powerful magnets to levitate above the tracks, eliminating friction and allowing for much higher speeds than traditional wheeled trains. Once operational, the new line will reduce travel time between Tokyo and Nagoya from approximately 100 minutes by conventional high-speed rail to just 40 minutes. Japanese rail companies are also in talks with several other countries, including the United States and India, about exporting their maglev technology for high-speed rail projects abroad.

transcript.heading: Conversation One (American Male + American Female)
paras: Man (Tom): Hey Sarah, do you have a minute? I need your advice about something. I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I can't decide between a cat and a dog.
Woman (Sarah): Oh, that's a big decision! Both make wonderful pets, but they're pretty different in terms of care and lifestyle. Do you have any idea which way you're leaning?

Man: That's the thing—I really like both. I grew up with dogs, so I know how loving and loyal they can be, but I work pretty long hours at the office, and I'm worried about leaving a dog home alone all day. Cats seem more independent, but I'm not sure if they're as affectionate.

Woman: That's a good point. Dogs definitely need more attention—they need to be walked at least twice a day, and they thrive on companionship. If you're gone 10-12 hours a day, a dog might get lonely or develop separation anxiety. Cats, on the other hand, are perfectly fine being left alone during the day as long as they have food, water, and a clean litter box. They do show affection, just in different ways—they might curl up next to you on the couch or greet you at the door.
Man: What about cost? I've heard pets can be pretty expensive with vet bills and everything.

Woman: Both can be costly, but generally, dogs tend to be more expensive overall. They eat more, grooming can be pricey depending on the breed, and there are expenses like doggy daycare if you travel. Cats are usually lower maintenance in that regard. But I will say—if you get a puppy or kitten, you should plan for initial vet visits, vaccinations, and spaying or neutering.
Man: Right, I hadn't thought about grooming. I also live in a small one-bedroom apartment. Does that matter?

Woman: Size is definitely a factor. A large dog breed would probably be miserable in a small apartment, but a small dog or a cat would do just fine. If you do go with a dog, I'd recommend adopting an older dog from a shelter rather than getting a puppy—they're often calmer and already house-trained.
Man: That's a really good suggestion. What about the adoption process? I've never adopted a pet before.

Woman: Most shelters have an application process where they ask about your living situation, work schedule, and previous pet experience. They want to make sure their animals go to good homes. There's usually an adoption fee, but that often includes spaying/neutering and initial vaccinations, so it's actually a pretty good deal. Let me know if you want me to send you links to a couple of good shelters in the area—I volunteer at one on weekends.
Man: That would be great, thanks! I think I need to do more research, but this has been really helpful.

Woman: That's a good point. I have my 7-year-old son coming too, so a matinee might actually be better for him—he gets restless if we're out too late. How much are tickets this year?
Man: They're 12 pounds for adults and 8 pounds for children and seniors. I think there's also a family ticket for two adults and two children that's 35 pounds, which saves a bit of money.

transcript.heading: Passage One (British Male)
paras: Urban beekeeping has grown in popularity over the past decade as more city residents become concerned about declining bee populations and interested in producing their own honey. What was once primarily a rural activity is now common in major cities around the world, with beehives appearing on rooftops, in community gardens, and even on apartment balconies. Many people are surprised to learn that cities can actually be excellent environments for honeybees. Urban areas often have a greater diversity of flowering plants than suburban or agricultural areas, thanks to parks, gardens, street trees, and window boxes. Additionally, cities typically use fewer pesticides than commercial farmland, creating a safer foraging environment for bees. Research from several universities has found that urban bees often produce more honey and are healthier than their rural counterparts. However, urban beekeeping does come with challenges. Beekeepers must be diligent about managing their hives to prevent swarming, which can alarm neighbors who are unfamiliar with bee behavior. They also need to ensure that bees have access to clean water and adequate forage throughout the growing season. Many cities have responded to the rise in urban beekeeping by creating guidelines and offering educational programs for new beekeepers. Some cities even offer incentives for installing hives on public buildings, recognizing that bees play a crucial role in pollinating urban plants and food crops. For many urban beekeepers, the hobby is not just about honey—it's about connecting with nature and contributing to environmental conservation in the middle of a busy city.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (American Female)
paras: The concept of emotional intelligence, often referred to as EQ, has become one of the most discussed topics in psychology and workplace management over the past 30 years. First popularized by psychologist Daniel Goleman in his 1995 book, emotional intelligence refers to the ability to recognize, understand, manage, and effectively use our own emotions, as well as the ability to recognize, understand, and respond appropriately to the emotions of others. Researchers typically break emotional intelligence into four key components. The first is self-awareness—the ability to accurately identify your own emotions as they occur and understand how they affect your thoughts and behavior. Self-aware people tend to have a realistic view of their strengths and weaknesses and are comfortable saying "I don't know" when they lack knowledge. The second component is self-management, which involves regulating your emotions, particularly in stressful situations. This includes staying calm under pressure, recovering quickly from setbacks, and avoiding impulsive decisions. The third component is social awareness, which includes empathy—the ability to understand another person's perspective and emotional state. Socially aware individuals are good at reading social cues and recognizing power dynamics in groups. The fourth component is relationship management, which involves using the other three skills to communicate clearly, resolve conflicts, inspire and influence others, and build strong personal and professional bonds. Studies have shown that emotional intelligence is a strong predictor of success in leadership positions, sometimes even more so than IQ or technical expertise. The good news is that unlike IQ, which remains relatively stable throughout life, emotional intelligence can be learned and developed with practice and feedback. Many companies now offer EQ training programs for their employees, particularly those in management roles.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Male)
paras: Community colleges, sometimes called junior colleges, play a unique and important role in higher education in the United States. Unlike four-year colleges and universities, which typically offer bachelor's degrees, community colleges primarily offer two-year associate degrees, certificate programs, and continuing education courses. One of the biggest advantages of community colleges is their accessibility. Tuition costs are typically much lower than at four-year institutions—often 50 to 70 percent less per credit hour—making higher education affordable for students who might not otherwise be able to attend college. Community colleges also have open enrollment policies, meaning that most students who have a high school diploma or equivalent are accepted, regardless of their previous academic performance. This makes them an excellent starting point for students who need to improve their academic skills before transferring to a four-year school, or for those who are unsure about their career direction. In recent years, many community colleges have developed strong partnerships with local businesses and industries to design certificate and training programs that directly prepare students for high-demand jobs in fields like healthcare, information technology, skilled trades, and public safety. These programs often take less time to complete than a traditional degree and have high job placement rates. Another important function of community colleges is serving non-traditional students—working adults, parents, career changers, and older students who need flexible scheduling options, including evening, weekend, and online classes. Many community colleges also offer basic education courses for adults who need to improve their literacy or earn a high school equivalency diploma, as well as English language classes for immigrants. As the cost of four-year colleges continues to rise and the job market demands more skilled workers, community colleges are likely to play an increasingly central role in American higher education and workforce development.
